storyPlan.premise: 3 Claude Code commands most people never use: /compact to shrink a long session without losing the thread, /rewind to undo the last changes, and plan mode (Shift+Tab) to see the plan before any file is touched. Show each one working.

plan.visualBrief: Three file cards break and glow orange, /rewind types into a terminal below, and an orange U-turn arrow sweeps over the files, turning them clean one by one.

scenes.vo: Claude Code just broke three files? One command undoes it.

plan.visualBrief: The terminal grows into a big Claude Code window while three empty numbered slots drop in above it one by one, landing on 3.

scenes.vo: It's one of three Claude Code commands most people never use.

plan.visualBrief: Slot 1 widens with /rewind, the command runs in the terminal and its last three edits roll back, then the three orange broken files below turn clean.

scenes.vo: First, slash rewind. Type it, and Claude Code undoes its last changes. Those three broken files? Clean again.

plan.visualBrief: Slot 2 widens with /compact, and a tall scrolling chat history squeezes into one short block while the thread line from first to last message stays whole and lights orange.

scenes.vo: Second, slash compact. When a session gets long and heavy, it shrinks it down, without losing the thread of what you're building.

plan.visualBrief: Slot 3 widens with Plan mode, the Shift and Tab keys press down, then a numbered plan unfolds in the terminal while the files beside it get orange padlocks.

scenes.vo: Third, plan mode. Press Shift Tab, and Claude shows you its plan first. Not a single file is touched until you're happy with it.

plan.visualBrief: The three filled slots shrink into a column on the left, a comment bubble pops up beside them, then a Follow button lights orange and pulses.

scenes.vo: Drop a comment if you want more Claude Code tips like these, and follow so you don't miss the next one.
